# Support matrix

Generated from `preflight/support-matrix.yml`, which is the single source of the preflight decision. Tiers: **supported** (full VM tests and reference GPU hardware), **tested** (full VM tests, GPU paths not hardware-tested), **experimental** (consent required), **unsupported**. A host's tier is the worst of its OS, architecture and environment tiers.

## Environments

| Class | Tier | Provider | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baremetal | supported | baremetal | — |
| wsl2 | supported | wsl2 | — |
| vm | supported | vm | Latency and resource measurements include virtualization overhead; the hypervisor is recorded in the fingerprint. |
| wsl1 | unsupported | — | WSL1 has no real Linux kernel; convert with 'wsl --set-version &lt;distro&gt; 2' |
| container | unsupported | — | The lab needs its own kernel features, systemd as PID 1, and nested container/VM capabilities |
| unknown | unsupported | — | Could not determine the environment reliably |

## Minimum hardware

Below *required* the host is unsupported; below *recommended* preflight warns.

| Resource | Required | Recommended |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory (GiB) | 16 | 24 |
| CPU threads | 8 | 16 |
| Free disk for /var/lib (GiB) | 150 | 400 |
| Free disk for /srv/pinka (GiB) | 100 | 500 |

## Core requirements

Failing any of these makes the host unsupported, unless a provider rule below resolves it as an operator action.

| Requirement | Values | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `systemd_pid1` | — | PID 1 must be systemd. |
| `cgroup2_unified` | — | Boot with the unified cgroup v2 hierarchy (systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1) or use a release that defaults to it. |
| `cgroup2_controllers` | cpu, cpuset, memory, io, pids | The cgroup v2 controllers cpu, cpuset, memory, io and pids must be available. |
| `dev_net_tun` | — | /dev/net/tun must exist (tun module or built-in); Tailscale needs it. |
| `kernel_features` | overlay, br_netfilter, nf_tables, veth | The kernel must provide overlay, br_netfilter, nf_tables and veth (built in or loadable). |
| `no_blocking_conflicts` | — | Resolve every blocking conflict listed above. |

## Storage

No quota-capable storage: neither btrfs nor LVM thin provisioning (dm_thin_pool) is available. A `dir` storage backend cannot enforce disk quotas, so disk-exhaustion scenarios would fill the host disk.

| Order | Feature | Backend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | btrfs_pool | btrfs |
| 2 | lvm_thin_pool | lvm |

## Optional features

| Feature | Requires | When missing | Only matters without | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpu_inference` | nvidia_gpu_usable, gpu_vram_gib_min: 8, gpu_compute_capability_min: 7.0 | degrade | — | No usable GPU: vLLM will not be installed; inference campaigns cannot run on this host. |
| `vm_targets` | kvm_usable | degrade | — | No KVM: VM-class scenarios (kernel-level faults) cannot run on this host. |
| `btrfs_pool` | btrfs_available | fallback | — | No btrfs: the Incus pool falls back to LVM thin provisioning. |
| `lvm_thin_pool` | dm_thin_pool_available | degrade | btrfs_pool | No LVM thin provisioning. |
| `dcgm_metrics` | environment_in: baremetal, vm, nvidia_driver_loaded | fallback | — | No DCGM: GPU metrics come from the nvidia-smi exporter. |

## Provider rules

| Provider | Kind | When | Resolves | Text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wsl2 | needs_action | wsl_conf_systemd: no | systemd_pid1 | Enable systemd in /etc/wsl.conf (the bootstrap can write it), then run 'wsl --terminate &lt;distro&gt;' from Windows and re-run bootstrap |
| wsl2 | warnings | wsl_interop_enabled: yes | — | Windows interop is enabled; the wsl2 provider will disable it |
| wsl2 | warnings | wsl_automount_enabled: yes | — | Windows drive automount is enabled; the wsl2 provider will disable it |
| baremetal | needs_action | secure_boot: enabled, nvidia_driver_installed: no, nvidia_gpu_present: yes, nvidia_driver_mode_in: auto, manual | — | Secure Boot is on: the NVIDIA DKMS module must be signed and a MOK enrolled at next boot. With install_nvidia_driver: auto, consent with --accept-mok-enrollment (or in the installer) and bootstrap installs the driver and imports the MOK; otherwise install the driver yourself. See docs/providers/baremetal.md |
| baremetal | planned action | the row above, and nvidia_driver_mode: auto, mok_enrollment_accepted: yes | — | Secure Boot is on: bootstrap installs the NVIDIA driver, imports a Machine Owner Key with your one-time password and stops with 76; reboot, enroll the key at the blue MOK Manager screen, then re-run bootstrap |
| vm | warnings | hypervisor_in: microsoft, vmware, oracle, kvm_usable: no | — | Nested virtualization unavailable in this hypervisor; VM-class targets disabled |

## Last test results

`make test-distros` ([How to test the distributions](how-to/test-distributions.md)) bootstraps the lab in a disposable VM per target, runs bootstrap a second time, which must change nothing, and then `pinka doctor --smoke`. A result counts for 90 days after its test date (*Valid until*); a target whose last result failed or has expired counts as untested.
